chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Umar ibn Hanzala, who said:
Dried sea bass (Rabeetha) were brought to me in a basket. So I went to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and asked him about it. He said: 'Eat it, for it has scales (skin/shell).'

key_terms.قِشْرٌ: Skins, scales, or shell (used here to denote the presence of scales which makes fish halal)

ai.seo_question: Is dried fish with scales permissible to eat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Umar ibn Hanzala consults Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding a dried fish, to which the Imam permits consumption based on the presence of *qishr* (scales). This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for establishing that the primary criterion for the permissibility of sea creatures is the presence of scales, distinguishing them from non-scaled marine life.
